title: Addition and Subtraction Facts to 20
seo_title: Grade 2 Addition and Subtraction Facts to 20 Worksheets (TEKS 2.4A)
standard_text: 2.4A recall basic facts to add and subtract within 20 with automaticity
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 addition and subtraction fact worksheets for Texas TEKS 2.4A: ten frames, doubles, make a ten, subtraction facts and fact stories. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Use doubles and make a ten.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Know the facts to 20 by heart. Use a strategy you know to find the rest.
  • Doubles: 7 + 7 = 14, so 7 + 8 = 15.
  • Make a ten: 9 + 5 = 10 + 4 = 14.
  • Think addition to subtract: 13 − 5 = ? because 5 + 8 = 13.

Examples

Example

8 + 6

8 + 2 = 10

10 + 4

Answer: 14

Example

15 − 7

7 + 8 = 15

Answer: 8

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting one too manyStart counting after the first number.
Mixing up + and −Read the sign before you start.
Not using a known factUse doubles and tens to help.

faq.a: Recall basic facts to add and subtract within 20 with automaticity.
Facts with two of the same number, like 6 + 6.

faq.q: How can a ten frame help?
faq.a: It shows how many more make 10.

items.q: How many counters are in the ten frame?
items.e: The top row is full: that is 5. The bottom row has 1. 5 + 1 = 6.

items.q: How many counters are in the ten frame?
items.e: The top row is full: that is 5. The bottom row has 4. 5 + 4 = 9.

items.q: How many counters are in the ten frame?
items.e: The top row is full: that is 5. The bottom row has 2. 5 + 2 = 7.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: A ten frame has 10 boxes. 8 boxes have counters, so 2 boxes are empty. 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: A ten frame has 10 boxes. 4 boxes have counters, so 6 boxes are empty. 4 + 6 = 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: A ten frame has 10 boxes. 3 boxes have counters, so 7 boxes are empty. 3 + 7 = 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: A ten frame has 10 boxes. 5 boxes have counters, so 5 boxes are empty. 5 + 5 = 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: A ten frame has 10 boxes. 2 boxes have counters, so 8 boxes are empty. 2 + 8 = 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: A ten frame has 10 boxes. 6 boxes have counters, so 4 boxes are empty. 6 + 4 = 10.

items.q: How many counters are there in all?
items.e: A full ten frame is 10. 10 + 3 = 13. That is 1 ten and 3 ones.

items.q: How many counters are there in all?
items.e: A full ten frame is 10. 10 + 6 = 16. That is 1 ten and 6 ones.

items.q: How many counters are there in all?
items.e: A full ten frame is 10. 10 + 8 = 18. That is 1 ten and 8 ones.

items.q: How many counters are there in all?
items.e: A full ten frame is 10. 10 + 5 = 15. That is 1 ten and 5 ones.
7 and 3 make 10. Count up from 7: 8, 9, 10. That is 3.
4 and 6 make 10. Count up from 4: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 6.
9 and 1 make 10. Count up from 9: 10. That is 1.
2 and 8 make 10. Count up from 2: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 8.
6 + 4 = 10. The others make 11, 9 and 12.
7 + 3 = 10. The others make 11, 9 and 12.
8 + 2 = 10. The others make 11, 9 and 12.

items.q: 4 + 4 = ?
items.e: 4 + 4 is a double. 4 + 4 = 8. A spider has 8 legs: 4 on each side.

items.q: 5 + 5 = ?
items.e: 5 + 5 is a double. 5 + 5 = 10. Two hands have 10 fingers: 5 and 5.

items.q: 6 + 6 = ?
items.e: 6 + 6 is a double. 6 + 6 = 12. An egg carton has 2 rows of 6 eggs: 12 eggs.
7 + 7 is a double. 7 + 7 = 14. Two weeks have 14 days: 7 and 7.
8 + 8 is a double. 8 + 8 = 16. 8 + 2 = 10, and 6 more is 16.
9 + 9 is a double. 9 + 9 = 18. 10 + 10 = 20. Take away 2, and you get 18.
6 + 6 = 12. 7 is 1 more than 6, so add 1 more: 12 + 1 = 13.

items.q: Use a double. 5 + 6 = ?
items.e: 5 + 5 = 10. 6 is 1 more than 5, so add 1 more: 10 + 1 = 11.
8 + 8 = 16. 9 is 1 more than 8, so add 1 more: 16 + 1 = 17.

items.q: Use a double. 4 + 5 = ?
items.e: 4 + 4 = 8. 5 is 1 more than 4, so add 1 more: 8 + 1 = 9.
7 + 7 = 14. 8 is 1 more than 7, so add 1 more: 14 + 1 = 15.

items.q: Which way uses a double to find 8 + 9?
items.e: 9 is 1 more than 8. So 8 + 9 is 8 + 8 and 1 more: 16 + 1 = 17.

items.q: Which way uses a double to find 7 + 6?
items.e: 7 is 1 more than 6. So 7 + 6 is 6 + 6 and 1 more: 12 + 1 = 13.

items.q: Which way uses a double to find 3 + 4?
items.e: 4 is 1 more than 3. So 3 + 4 is 3 + 3 and 1 more: 6 + 1 = 7.

items.q: Which way uses a double to find 6 + 5?
items.e: 6 is 1 more than 5. So 6 + 5 is 5 + 5 and 1 more: 10 + 1 = 11.

items.q: Camila knows 8 + 8 = 16. How can she find 8 + 7?
items.e: 7 is 1 less than 8. So 8 + 7 is 1 less than 8 + 8: 16 − 1 = 15.
6 + 6 = 12. 8 is 2 more than 6, so add 2: 12 + 2 = 14. Or use the middle number: 7 + 7 = 14.
5 + 5 = 10. 7 is 2 more than 5, so add 2: 10 + 2 = 12. Or use the middle number: 6 + 6 = 12.
7 + 7 = 14. 9 is 2 more than 7, so add 2: 14 + 2 = 16. Or use the middle number: 8 + 8 = 16.
4 + 4 = 8. 6 is 2 more than 4, so add 2: 8 + 2 = 10. Or use the middle number: 5 + 5 = 10.

items.q: Move counters to fill the top ten frame. What is 9 + 4?
items.e: Move 1 counter up. Now the top frame has 10, and 3 are left. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Move counters to fill the top ten frame. What is 8 + 5?
items.e: Move 2 counters up. Now the top frame has 10, and 3 are left. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Move counters to fill the top ten frame. What is 9 + 7?
items.e: Move 1 counter up. Now the top frame has 10, and 6 are left. 10 + 6 = 16.

items.q: Move counters to fill the top ten frame. What is 8 + 6?
items.e: Move 2 counters up. Now the top frame has 10, and 4 are left. 10 + 4 = 14.

Think addition: 8 + 5 = 13. So 13 − 8 = 5.
Think addition: 9 + 6 = 15. So 15 − 9 = 6.
Think addition: 7 + 5 = 12. So 12 − 7 = 5.
Think addition: 8 + 8 = 16. So 16 − 8 = 8.
Think addition: 6 + 8 = 14. So 14 − 6 = 8.
Start at 12 and count back 3: 11, 10, 9. Do not count 12 itself. 12 − 3 = 9.
Start at 11 and count back 2: 10, 9. Do not count 11 itself. 11 − 2 = 9.
Start at 15 and count back 3: 14, 13, 12. Do not count 15 itself. 15 − 3 = 12.
Start at 17 and count back 2: 16, 15. Do not count 17 itself. 17 − 2 = 15.
16 − 6 = 10. You must take away 9 in all, and 6 is done. So take away 3 more: 10 − 3 = 7.
13 − 3 = 10. You must take away 5 in all, and 3 is done. So take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.
11 − 1 = 10. You must take away 4 in all, and 1 is done. So take away 3 more: 10 − 3 = 7.

items.q: Which fact is in the same family as 6 + 9 = 15?
items.e: The family of 6, 9 and 15: 6 + 9 = 15, 9 + 6 = 15, 15 − 6 = 9, 15 − 9 = 6. Only 15 − 9 = 6 uses all three numbers.

items.q: Which fact is in the same family as 7 + 5 = 12?
items.e: The family of 7, 5 and 12: 7 + 5 = 12, 5 + 7 = 12, 12 − 7 = 5, 12 − 5 = 7. Only 12 − 7 = 5 uses all three numbers.

items.q: Which fact is in the same family as 8 + 9 = 17?
items.e: The family of 8, 9 and 17: 8 + 9 = 17, 9 + 8 = 17, 17 − 8 = 9, 17 − 9 = 8. Only 9 + 8 = 17 uses all three numbers.
Count up from 9 to 10, then to 15: 9 + 1 = 10, 10 + 5 = 15. 1 + 5 = 6, so the missing number is 6.
Count up from 7 to 10, then to 13: 7 + 3 = 10, 10 + 3 = 13. 3 + 3 = 6, so the missing number is 6.
Count up from 8 to 10, then to 12: 8 + 2 = 10, 10 + 2 = 12. 2 + 2 = 4, so the missing number is 4.
Count up from 6 to 10, then to 14: 6 + 4 = 10, 10 + 4 = 14. 4 + 4 = 8, so the missing number is 8.
Think addition: 7 + 8 = 15. Check: 15 − 7 = 8. 1 is wrong because 8 − 7 = 1 goes the other way.

Think addition: 9 + 8 = 17. So 17 − 9 = 8.
Think addition: 3 + 8 = 11. So 11 − 3 = 8.
Start with 8. Take 2 from the 4 to make 10: 8 + 2 = 10. Then add the 2 left: 10 + 2 = 12.
Think addition: 7 + 7 = 14. So 14 − 7 = 7. 7 + 7 = 14 is a double.
Think addition: 5 + 7 = 12. So 12 − 5 = 7.

items.q: Luis has 8 red beads and 5 blue beads. How many beads does he have?
items.e: Put the two groups together, so add. Take 2 from the 5 to make 10: 8 + 2 = 10. Then add the 3 left: 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: There are 15 birds on a fence. 7 birds fly away. How many birds are left?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract: 15 − 7 = 8. Think: 7 + 8 = 15.

items.q: Mia has 9 toy cars. She gets 3 more. How many toy cars does she have now?
items.e: Put the two groups together, so add. Take 1 from the 3 to make 10: 9 + 1 = 10. Then add the 2 left: 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: There are 12 apples in a bag. Marcus uses 4 for a pie. How many apples are left?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract: 12 − 4 = 8. Think: 4 + 8 = 12.

items.q: A tank has 6 fish. The class puts in 7 more fish. How many fish are in the tank now?
items.e: Put the two groups together, so add. Start with 7. Take 3 from the 6 to make 10: 7 + 3 = 10. Then add the 3 left: 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Liam has 16 stickers. He gives 9 to a friend. How many stickers does he have left?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract: 16 − 9 = 7. Think: 9 + 7 = 16.

items.q: Carlos read 7 pages on Monday. He read 7 pages on Tuesday. How many pages did he read in all?
items.e: Put the pages together, so add: 7 + 7 = 14. It is a double.

items.q: There are 11 kids at the park. 5 kids go home. How many kids are still at the park?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract: 11 − 5 = 6. Think: 5 + 6 = 11.

items.q: Emma has 9 crayons. She wants 15 crayons. How many more crayons does she need?
items.e: Count up from 9 to 15: 9 + 6 = 15. So 15 − 9 = 6.

items.q: Diego has 13 shells. Harper has 6 shells. How many more shells does Diego have than Harper?
items.e: Find the difference: 13 − 6 = 7. Think: 6 + 7 = 13.

items.q: There are 14 cookies on a plate. The kids eat some. Now 8 cookies are left. How many cookies did they eat?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract: 14 − 8 = 6. Think: 8 + 6 = 14.

items.q: Some ducks are in a pond. 4 more ducks come. Now there are 11 ducks. How many ducks were there at first?
items.e: Take away the 4 ducks that came: 11 − 4 = 7. Check: 7 + 4 = 11.

items.q: There are 17 children on a bus. 8 children get off. How many children are on the bus now?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract: 17 − 8 = 9. Think: 8 + 9 = 17.

items.q: Noah picks 6 flowers. Lucia picks 8 flowers. How many flowers do they pick in all?
items.e: Put the two groups together, so add. Start with 8. Take 2 from the 6 to make 10: 8 + 2 = 10. Then add the 4 left: 10 + 4 = 14.
